parties:
Fazlur Rahman & Co Private Ltd ------ Plaintiff
vs. 
MV Chosun Hopi and anothers ------ Defendants
full_judgment:
This Admiralty suit filed by Fazlur Rahman and Company Pvt. Ltd. On 24-7-1997 for realization of compensation for short landing of goods valued at 1,21,61,175 has been heard in presence of both the parties and now disposed of by this judgment. 
2. It has been asserted in the plaint that the plaintiff Company imports Soda Ash Light and other chemical product for the purpose of business in course of such business the plaintiff imported from China 9420 MT and 800 MT Soda Ash Light under Letter of Credit dated 16-4-1997 and 21-4-1997 respectively which has been carried on board by the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Chosun Hope'. The shipment was acknowledged by the Bill of Lading dated 22-5-1997. The shipment was procured under Invoice dated 22-5-1997. There is clause in the Charter Party that the owner guarantees, that the vessel will arrive at the discharge port of Chittagong by 11th June 1997 (wrongly printed 11th May 1997 in the Bill of Lading) otherwise the owner to be responsible for consequences. The vessel arrived late at the discharge port and the Bill of Entry was submitted by the plaintiff to the Customs Authority on or about 6-7-1997. But in the meantime the government fixed 2.5% development surcharge on the import of this type of cargo. The defendant No. 1 vessel started unloading the cargo at Chittagong Port and when it Has almost, finished the discharge of the cargo, it appears that the vessel will deliver less cargo then received on board at the loading Port as stevedores and the clearing agents of the plaintiff apprehended on the basis of the report dated 24-7-1997. Thereafter it appears that the vessel has short delivered 360 MT of Soda Ash Light.-The plaintiff prayed for Decree for compensation on the basis of the market value of 360 MT of Soda Ash Light @ Taka 12,005 per MT and also compensation for late delivery for which a development surcharge was imposed upon the Cargo, totaling an amount for Taka 1,27,61,175 against the defendant Nos. 1-4 and also for a decree for pendent lite interest (a) 20% per annum till realization of the decrial amount and in case of failure to satisfy the prospective decree by the defendant amicably, than to sell the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' and to apply its proceeds towards decreetal dues of the plaintiff. 
3. On 20-7-1997 the plaintiff obtained an order for amendment of the plaint, whereupon the plaintiff inserted further statement of fact that there was an agreement in between the plaintiff and the carriers that the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' would arrived the Chittagong Port before 12-6-1997 and if it failed to arrive by that date and the plaintiff is forced to give Bank Guarantee to the Customs Authority for 2.5% development surcharge on the cargo, the owner of the vessel undertook to reimburse the same. As market price of Soda Ash Light was plummeting so the owner guaranteed the plaintiff that the vessel will arrived by 19-6-1997. But as the vessel arrived on 6-7-1997 the plaintiff was in a loss of market price of Taka 1,000 per MT an as a result of such loss the plaintiff suffers loss about Taka 10,22,000 and as it appears that actual short landing of the Cargo is 8 MT than loss of 8 MTs Cargo comes to an amount of Taka 96,040 and also for damage for late delivery and imposition of development surcharge which further comes to Taka 24,45,135. The plaintiff also amended the plaint for the second time in paragraph No. 8 and the claim has been enhanced to Taka 1,27,61,175. 
4. The defendant Nos. 1, 3 and 4 are the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope', he owner and person interested in the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' and the local agent of the vessel respectively. The vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' was arrested on the prayer of the plaintiff and upon furnishing Bank Guarantee for Taka 32,00,000 the same was released from the arrest. The Ocean Wave Shipping Ltd entered appearance in this suit and contested the same by filing written statement on 10-3-1999. It has been asserted in the written statement that the suit is not maintainable in this Admiralty Court; that the plaintiff has no locus standi to file this suit and the suit is bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of parties and on the principle of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence and also denied all the material allegations made in the plaint. It has been asserted further by the defendants that the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' loaded the cargo of the plaintiff at the Lian Youngang Port, China for discharging the same at Chittagong, Bangladesh and accordingly, the said vessel sailed from the loading port from China on 29-5-1997 and arrived at Chittagong on 20-6-1997 and there was no delay on the arrival of the vessel. It has been denied that the owners had any contract will the plaintiff that if there has been any delay in arrival of the vessel, the plaintiff should seek remedy from the supplier, as there cannot be any specific time within which the ocean going vessel will arrive at the discharge port since the vessel has to pass an ocean from where the same may face enormous hazard including act of god/peril of sea/accident or mechanical trouble. In the instant case the statement of facts of the deck log book will reveal that there was no unreasonable delay or any delay for the vessel to arrive by 26-6-1997. The date alleged by the plaintiff in the charter party cannot be binding date as alleged by the plaintiff as has been provided in the charter party and accordingly the allegations, against the defendants for late arrival of the vessel is not tenable in the eye of law and facts. The owner of the vessel never undertook to discharge the cargo with the consignee within the fixed specific time. The vessel sailed from the port of China with the cargo of the plaintiff in the same condition as was loaded and arrived at Chittagong Port on 26-6-1997 and it plaintiff was owning to the negligees of the plaintiff that the plaintiff failed to submits that Bill of Entry before the Customs authority within 30-6-1997 against the imported cargo and due to delay in submitting the Bill of Entry before 30-6-1997, the plaintiff might have been effected by the development surcharge on the imported cargo which has been effected from the date of tabling of the Finance Bill in the Parliament for which the defendants cannot be liable. The plaintiff had to pay the development surcharge of 2.5% and the same would be recoverable by the plaintiff through marketing of the goods by inclusion of the same with the sale price. The plaintiff also filed two Writ Petitions challenging the imposition of the development surcharge upon his cargo and he did not pay the surcharge. The vessel in the meantime completed discharge of the cargo and as per final discharge report only 8 MT i.e. 212 Bags of cargo were found to be short landed which has been certified by the Master of the ship and such shortage cannot be treated as short landing of the cargo as against the huge quantity of bangs carried by the vessel and therefore, the claim of the plaintiff on this ground is not tenable in the eye of law. The plaintiff illegally obtained the order of arrest of the vessel and the owner of the vessel has suffered irreparable financial loss and damage and, as such, the plaintiff reserves the right to claim for the losses and damage from the defendant. Although the vessel has completed the discharge of the cargo on 25-7-1997 it was detained due to illegal arrest order. The suit being not maintainable and liable to be dismissed, the Bank Guarantee submitted by the defendant, being No. LG /1501 /1997/1264 dated 7-9-1997 for an amount of Taka 32,00,000 issued by ANZ Grindlays Bank, Dhaka is liable to be returned to the defendants. 
5. Upon examination of the pleading of the parties the following issues were framed by the Court on 24-4-1999. 
(1) Is the suit maintainable under Admiralty Jurisdiction? 
(2) Has the plaintiff any cause of action against these defendants? 
(3)  Did the defendant ship arrived in reasonable time? If not then to what extent is the ship responsible? 
(4) Is the suit bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of the parties?
(5) Is the suit barred under the principles of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence? 
(6) Was there any damage and short landing of the cargo as alleged by the plaintiff? 
(7) Has the plaintiff suffered any losses and damages? If so, are these defendants liable for the same? 
(8) Is the plaintiff entitled to any decree against these defendants? If so, to what extent?

8. The learned Senior Advocate Dr M Zahir along with Mr Ezaz Rahman represented the plaintiff in the suit while the learned Advocate Mr Muhammad Ohiullah along with Mr Fida M Kamal, Senior Counsel appeared on behalf of the defendants. 
9. We have heard the learned Advocate on their respective arguments, examined the different exhibits, dispositions, the assertion made in the plaint and in the written statement and also examined the material on record. We have also considered the argument advanced at the Bar. 
10. The plaint is ill drafted. The actual facts of the plaintiff claim comes from the documents as they have been exhibited. Upon meticulous examination of the plaintiff's documents, it appears that the plaintiff Messrs Fazlur Rahman & Company Pvt. Ltd. opened Letter of Credit in favour of Swiss Singapore Overseas Enterprise Pte Ltd. for import 10,200 MT Soda Ash Light upon the Sell Contract being No. SSOE/051A/97-98 dated 12-4-1997 dated Sale contract No. SSOE /063A /97-98 dated 17-4-1997 which were marked Exhibit I to 1(a). Upon such sale contract the seller/supplier Swiss Singapore Overseas Enterprise Pte Ltd. Chartered at ocean going vessel from its owner of 'MV You Hang' Navigation (SE), the carrier, whose deponent owner was Swiss Singapore Overseas Enterprise Pte Ltd and the Charter party was executed on Gencon format for the carriage of the plaintiff's consignment of 10,200 MT Soda Ash Light by the said vessel 'MV You Hang', stipulating the date of ready to load on 12-5-1997. Thereafter, for the reason best known to them, they said Charter Party Agreement was amended thrice by the addendum dated 14-5-1997 and 23-5-1997 and also on 25-3-1997 through which the vessel was changed from 'MV You Hang' to 'MV Chosun Hope' and also the date of loading by the date 20-5-1997. Thereafter the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' loaded the plaintiff's cargo and sailed from the load port Lian Yungang on 29-5-1997 after issuing eleven Bills of Lading, marked as Exhibit 2 series. Thereafter the vessel confronted with the mechanical problem on 1-6-1997 on the high sea, for which the engine was stopped and that being repaired within the same day it resume its journey on 2-6-1997 when it reached Hongkong Port at 2.00 hour on 6-6-1997 and on the same day it resumed its journey and anchored at Singapore Port on 14-6-1997 wherein the vessel was waited upto 19-6-1997 for the instruction from the charterer. Thereafter, upon resuming the journey, the vessel reached the outer anchorage of the Chittagong Port on 28-6-1997 at 13.32 hours, but as no Nos. (Notice of readiness) was received from the consignee up to 13-7-1997, the pilot of the Chittagong Port Authority boarded the vessel on 13-7-1997 and the same berthed at Jetty No. 8 on the same day at 9-00 hours. Thereafter the discharge of the cargo commenced immediately which was ultimately concluded on 26-7-1997. 
11. These state of affairs, as aforesaid, appears to be admitted by the defendant. It has been asserted by, the defendant that the plaintiff filed the Bill of Entry on 6-7-1997, and without waiting for the conclusion of the discharge filed the instant suit on 24-7-1997 with a false claim that 360 MT of the Cargo will be short landed. Actually there was no short landing of the Cargo as 8 MT Cargo, equivalent to 212 bags cannot be treated as short landing against huge quantity of cargo, i.e. 10,220 MT. The statement of fact as appears from deck log book shows that there was no delay of the vessel in arriving at discharge port. The plaintiff by getting order in Writ Petition did not pay the development surcharge and the plaintiff had not suffered any loss and the instant suit caused irreparable loss and injury to the defendant, as the vessel was illegally arrested by the plaintiff. 
12. Upon the aforesaid facts, as appears from the exhibited documents filed by the parties, the issue of the suit as per the plaintiff's claim for recovery of compensation for short landing of 8 MT goods and for imposition of development surcharge on the goods and also consequence loss is required to be recast in the following matter, as the defendants did not emphasis on the some of the issues as framed earlier in this suit; 
(1) Is the suit is maintainable in its present form & manner? 
(2) Has the plaintiff any cause of action against the defendants? 
(3) Has the plaintiff any agreement with the defendants for arrival of the consignment on or before 19-6-1997? 
(4) Did the defendants violate any of the terms of the charter party agreement to discharge the consignment within the reasonable period? 
(5) Are the defendants liable for the damaged caused to the plaintiff for imposition of development surcharge and on the plummeting of the price of the goods? 
(6) Is the plaintiff is entitled to the decree as prayer for? 
(7) What are the other relief or relieves of which the plaintiff is entitled to? 
We will now dispose of the issues in seriatim. 
Issue No. 1: 
13. The learned Senior Advocate Mr Fida M Kamal, on the point of maintainability of this suit in this jurisdiction, which taken this Court through the admission made by the PW 1, the Managing Director of the plaintiff's company to the extent that he did not retired the shipping documents from, the Bank at any point of time and the endorsement on the Exhibit 2 series i.e. on the Bills of Lading, to the extent that it was "attested for the. Customs assessment purpose only" and not for clearance of the goods strenuously argued referring the decision of the case Messrs Shahnaj Traders vs 'MV Sletter' reported in 7 BLT (AD) 381 that as the plaintiff did not retire the shipping documents he is not a party aggrieved to institute the instant Admiralty Suit. Further the plaintiff not being the consignee of the goods, as appears from the Bills of Leading, he cannot challenge the short landing and so called late arrival of the vessel and consequently the business loss, against the carrier as has been done in the instant case. The learned Senior Advocate Mr Fida M Kamal argued that only the consignee can institute an Admiralty Suit on the grounds of shot landing, late arrival of the ship and consequently the business loss of the consignee and since the Sonali Bank is the consignee of the cargo in the instant import, the plaintiff has got no locus standi to institute the instant suit. 
14. On the other hand the learned Senior Advocate Dr M Zahir simply refuted the argument by submitting that the plaintiff being the actual importer of the goods as the notified party, as appears from the Bills of Lading and, as such, he being the beneficiary of the consignment has every authority to institute legal proceeding .on any grievance against the carrier. He further argued that the plaintiff actually took delivery of the goods from the Customs Authority through the LIM Account with Sonali Bank and, as such, it cannot be said that plaintiff has never retired the shipping documents. The endorsement on Exhibit No. 2 was nothing but an endorsement at the relevant time and as the original documents were submitted to the Customs authority, the plaintiff exhibited the Exhibit No. 2 as it was available to him.
15. Upon examination of the reported case of 7 BLT (AD) 381 it appears that their lordships on the apex Court when deciding the point who can file the suit in the Admiralty jurisdiction held as under: 
"An Admiralty Suit can be field by the owner or consignee or assignee of any bill of lading of any goods carried by ship for damage done to the goods or any part thereby by negligence or misconduct of the owner, master or crews. Under Section 6 the owner or consignee or assignee of any bill of lading can file an Admiralty Suit. It is true that the plaintiff has filed the suit claiming the amount for loss/damages of the consignment by the negligence of defendant No. 1 or its master and crews but all disputes from the port of loading to the port of delivery arose out of various contracts. So it is not correct to say that the claim of compensation for damages is independent of any contract. Thus, the learned Admiralty Judge was correct in holding that the suit is not maintainable in Admiralty jurisdiction on this Court as well." 
16. The plaintiff of the reported suit imported 15,153,868 MT granular Triple Super Phosphate by opening Letter of Credit through its banker United Commercial Bank Limited in favour of the supplier Messrs Seminole Fertilizer Corporation, on condition to deliver the consignment at Chittagong/Mongla Port ocean going vessel. Defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Sletter' took the tusk of shipment of the plaintiff consignment of discharge the said consignment at the discharge port at its own risk and arrangement. After he arrival of the said Mother vessel at the discharge Port, the local agents of the defendant No. 1 arranged to discharge the cargo through lighterage vessel i.e. by a sister vessel 'MV Queen of Diamond' to the Mongla Port, which having been faced with mechanical trouble, the discharge was not done in time and the vessel sunk and went in the sea due to force major situation for which the plaintiff of that suit never retired the shipping documents as it was not beneficial to the said plaintiff. The shipping documents were never assigned to the importer and upon the facts and circumstances of that case their lordships held that as the plaintiff did not retire the Bills of Lading at any point of time, and the title to the goods remained with the bank the importer cannot institute suit claiming compensation against the defendants. 
17. But the facts and circumstances of the instant case show otherwise. The plaintiff of the instant suit at the very initial stage obtained the photocopy of the set of shipping documents from the consignee Sonali Bank which was issued for the purpose of customs assessment and not for the clearance of the goods which has been exhibited as Exhibit No. 2 series. But from the evidence on record it appears that upon a LIM account maintained in favour of the plaintiff by the Sonali Bank the said goods were ultimately taken delivery by the Sonali Bank from the Port authority and the plaintiff had further taken delivery of the consignment from the Sonali Bank as and when he could furnish the part payment for respective price to the said Bank. Therefore the facts and circumstances of the case of the referred case being different, the said principle as reported in 7 BLT (AD) 381 is not applicable in the instant case. 
18. The plaintiff being the actual importer of the goods upon a LIM account with the L/C opening Bank, the beneficial ownership in the consignment remains with the plaintiff the actual importer, subject to payment of loan money to the Bank and the L/C opening Bank remains a sham consignee till the entire loan money is repaid by the importer. Since in the instant case the importer ultimately took the delivery of the goods through the L/C opening Bank, this Court finds that the importer has locus standi to institute the instant suit as plaintiff in the Admiralty jurisdiction of this Court to recover any compensation in respect of such goods. Therefore, the issue No. 1 is disposed of in favour of the plaintiff. 
Issues No. 2-7 
19. The issue Nos. 2-7 having founded on the same facts and circumstance are taken together for disposal for the sake of brevity and convenience. 
20. The plaintiff brought the suit on the cause of action, inter alia, that ultimately 8 MT of imported goods were short landed for which he suffered loss and further that he has an agreement with the carrier that the ship, through which the plaintiff consignment will be carried, shall reach the Chittagong Port on 11-6-1997. But ship failed to reach by the said stipulated date and arrived at the discharged port on 7-7-1997 and since the Government through the Finance Bill 1997 imposed the development surcharge @ 2.5% on the importation of Soda Ash Light, the plaintiff had to undergo additional expenses on the said count and since the ship arrived late the price of the Soda Ash Light having plummeted, the plaintiff further suffered business loss on the whole of the consignment. Therefor the compensation has been claimed upon the following four heads: 
1. Short landing of 8.48 MT goods, 
2. Violation of contract of reach by 11-6-1997. 
3. Loss due to payment of development surcharge. 
4. Business loss due to plummeting of market price.
21. Upon these points the plaintiff adduced evidence of two PW's and marked exhibit several documents. PW 1 is the Managing Director of the plaintiff company who categorically claimed that the plaintiff has an agreement with the defendants that the ship will arrive at Chittagong Port by 11-6-1997. In support of such claim the plaintiff relied on the Charter Party Agreement Exhibit-3. Upon examination of the Exhibit 3, it appears that the said Charter Party Agreement has been executed by the supplier of the consignment of Soda Ash Light Messrs Swiss Singapore Obverses Enterprise Pte Ltd Singapore with the deponent owner group of the vessel Messrs PR Marketing Pte Ltd. Which reveals that one ocean going vessel 'MV You Hang' will carry the consignment of the plaintiff from the port Liang yang, China to Chittagong Port. Nowhere within the four corners of the Charter Party, along with the rider clause it revealed that there is any stipulation that the vessel will reach the Chittagong Port within 11-6-1997. But the 1st addendum annexed to the Charter Party dated 14-5-1997 made an amendment to the Charter Party to the extent of changing the vessel from 'MV You Hang' to 'MV Chosun Hope which also amended the Charter party by inserting Clause No. 4 in the following manner: 
"The owners are to instruct the master to proceed with all dispatch to the load port in order to arrive within the lay can agree and on completion of loading to proceed directly and with all dispatch to the discharge port at maximum speed in order to reach the discharge port within about the 3rd, 4th January, 1997." 
22. The addendum No. 2 dated 23-5-1997 annexed to the Charter Party further stipulated. 
"owners guarantee that the vessel will arrive the discharge port of Chittagong by the 11th May 1997 weather permitting and subject to the vessel completing loading by the 27th May 1997 at the load port otherwise owners to be responsible for all consequences thereon." 
23. Addendum No. 3 dated 23-5-1997 annexed to the Charter Party further stipulated that:
"owners guarantee that the vessel will arrive the discharge port of Chittagong by the 11th May 1997 weather permitting and subject to the vessel completing loading by the 28th May 1997 at the load port otherwise owners to be responsible for All consequences thereof." 
24. The plaintiff relies on these amended stipulations made by the addendum Nos. 2 and 3 to the extent that the ship will arrive at Chittagong Port by a certain date which the plaintiff alleged in the plaint only, to have been wrongly mentioned in the addendum Nos. 2 and 3 as 11th May 1997 in place of 11th June 1997. It has been asserted in the plaint itself, at paragraph No. 3, that the date 11th June, 1997 has been wrongly printed as 11th May 1997. PW 1 in this respect, in his examination in chief, categorically evidenced that "there is a clause in the charter party that the ship will arrive at Port by 11th May 1997" and nowhere within the four corners of his examination-in-chief or in examination-in-cross he has said anything that the said date 11th May 1997 has been wrongly mentioned in the charter party addendum Nos. 2 and 3 in place on 11th June 1997. 
25. On the other hand, the DW 1 in his examination-in-chief categorically stated as to the said addendum that "there is a mistake in the addendum. In place of 11th May 1997 it should be 11th July 1997. Therefore, it appears that the date of arrival of the ship at the discharge part, as alleged to have been agreed upon by the owners of the ship with the Charterer has become disputed. 
26. The learned Senior Advocate Dr M Zahir argued that admittedly the ship loaded the plaintiffs cargo on 27-05-1997 and as such the natural presumption of its date of arrival at Chittagong Port will be within 10-12 days thereafter and therefore, the dated to be presumed, as incorporated in addendum of the Charter Party, is 11th June, 1997. 
27. It appears that from the addendum No. 1 that the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' is younger in age and although none of the parties have adduced any evidence as to the maximum speed of the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope', yet from the DW weight of the vessel and other attending facts and circumstances of the case and also from the materials on record it appears that such a younger ocean going vessel can proceed with a maximum speed of 9-12 nautical miles per hour. Exhibit 'A' is the lay time statement of facts and the Exhibit 'B' is the copy of deck log book of the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' filed by the defendants which being uncomforted, shows that the vessel commenced its journey from port Liang Youngang, China, on 29-5-1997 at 21-30 hours which stopped on the high sea on 1-6-1997 at night 00-45 hours for the purpose of its repairing to the engine and later resumed its journey on 16-46 hours on 2-6-1997. Thereafter, it anchored at Hongkong Port for an inspection on 6-6-1997 at 02-00 hours wherefrom it resumed journey on the same date at 15-00 hours and reached Singapore Port on 14-6-1997 at 07-10 hours, where it waited for Charterer's instruction upon 19-45 hours of 19-6-1996. Thereafter it resumed its journey to reach outer anchorage of Chittagong Port on 26-6-1997 at 13-32 hours. 
28. From the aforesaid Exhibit 'B', it appears that the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' traveled about 4,049.6 nautical miles from Liang Youngang Port, China, to the outer anchorage of Chittagong Port. It further appears that although it took 28 days to reach Chittagong but actually it was on the high sea on its journey for about 18 days to cover a length of 4049.6 nautical miles which shows that it covered 225 nautical miles per day (24 hours) at a speed of 9.75 nautical miles per hour. This speed, as appears from the materials on record, certifies conformity to the expected speed from the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope'. Therefore, the date as mentioned in the charter party cannot be presumed to be 11-6-1997 as the parties had in their mind the bad weather, the peril of the sea and other attending circumstances whether shall not allow the ship to reach the discharge port within 11-6-1997 i.e. only within 13 day after. Therefore, the natural conclusion as to the date which ought to have been mentioned in the charter party addendum appears to be 11-7-1997 and not 11-6-1997 as alleged by the plaintiff. The time consumed for taking instruction from the charterer cannot be treated as negligence of the defendant and that same cannot be taken as a ground for late arrival. 
29. Therefore, it appears that the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope' has not reached late in the discharge port and used its maximum speed and dispatch to reach discharge port within the stipulated period as made in the addendum of the charter party. 
30. The learned Senior Advocate Dr M Zahir while argued on the point of imposition of development surcharge through the Finance Bill, 1997 drawn the attention of this Court to the fact that if the vessel reached the port prior to 30-6-1997 the plaintiff would not have suffered the loss on the count of imposition of development surcharge on the consignment. 
31. But the leaned Senior Advocate Mr Fida M Kamal as against such arguments relied on two points. Firstly he argued that the provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1933 provides for immediate collection of any duty proposed to be imposed by the Finance Bill and accordingly the proposed development surcharge would have been collected from the date when the bill would have been tabled in the Parliament. On the Second point the learned Senior Advocate Mr Fida M Kamal argued that the plaintiff seems to have obtained relief from payment of development surcharge through the Writ Petition No. 4120 of 1997 and, as such, the plaintiff suffered no loss on the said count. 
32. It appears that the plaintiff has challenged the imposition of development surcharge on his instant importation of Soda Ash Light in Writ Petition No. 4120 of 1997 and although at the issuance of the Rule in the said Writ Petition, he was directed to furnish Bank Guarantee in order to take release of the consignment, yet on the making of the Rule absolute, the plaintiff was exonerated from the payment of the said development surcharge although the learned Senior Advocate Dr M Zahir informed this Court that the said judgment is now under appeal before the Hon'ble Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. Therefore, this Court finds that the plaintiff did not suffer any loss s yet on the count of imposition of development surcharge on the consignment of Soda Ash Light as imported through the defendant's vessel which reached Chittagong Port on 26-6-1997. 
33. The learned Senior Advocate Dr M Zahir while taking this Court to the claim of the plaintiff as to the business loss alleged to have been suffered due to the late arrival of the vesel at Chittagong Port, drawn the attention of this Court to the certificate issued by the Narayangonj Chamber of Commerce Exhibit No. 7 certifying the price of Soda Ash Light at the relevant time. But as this Court has already found that there was no late arrival of the vessel as per stipulation of the charter party, this Court is reluctant to enter into the propriety of the said Exhibit No. 7 and consequently the argument which appears to be not tenable in the facts and circumstances of the case. 
34. Therefore, the issue Nos. 2 to 7 is disposed of in favor of the defendants and against the plaintiff. 
Issue No. 8 
35. It appears that admittedly 8.48 MT of Soda Ash Light has been short landed from the vessel 'MV Chosun Hope'. The learned Senior Advocate Mr Fida M Kamal argued that while the entire consignment was of 10,220 MT having 2,55,500 bags, the short landing of 8.48 MT is so negligible as against the entire quantity of the consignment that it cannot be a claim for compensation. He further argued that such a short landing has been caused due to the negligent action on behalf of stevedore engaged by a the plaintiff and therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled to get any compensation in respect of the alleged short landing. 
36. We are unable to accept the argument. Admittedly the plaintiff has loaded 10,220 MT of the consignment of Soda Ash light having 2,55,500 bags in total as appears from the Bills of Lading Exhibit 2 (series) Therefore the defendant vessel is liable to discharge the same quantity of the consignment and is not allowed to rely upon any negligence on the part of the stevedores, either engaged by the plaintiff or the Chittagong Port Authority. Further the defendant could not prove the allegation that the plaintiff has engaged stevedore who was negligent in discharging the cargo from the vessel. Therefore, this Court finds that the defendants are liable to compensate the plaintiff in respect of the short landed goods amounting to 8.48 MT i.e. 212 bags of the Soda Ash light. 
37. So far the price of the said short landed good is concerned it appears that the plaintiff relied on the certificate issued by the Narayangonj Chamber of Commerce, Exhibit 7. Although the propriety of Exhibit No. 7 was challenged by the defendants but so far the question of ascertainment of the price of the cargo at the relevant time is concerned, the learned Senior Advocate Mr Fida M Kamal did not opposite the proposition to rely upon it. Therefore it appears to this Court that on 6-6-1997 the China origin Soda Ash Light was pried at Taka 12,500 per MT at export Chittagong. Therefore, it will be reasonable to decide that the plaintiff is entitled to recover from the defendant the compensation of 8.48 MT of Soda Ash Light @ Taka 12,500 per Metric Tons which comes to a total amount of Taka 1,06,250. Since the said loss occurred due to the defendants' negligence in discharging the consignment from the ship and remaining unpaid for the last 13 years the plaintiff is entitled to recover the compensation with interest @ 18% per annum which will meet the ends of justice. The defendant since never expressed his intention to pay off this lawful claim of the plaintiff, it is also liable to pay the cost of this suit to the plaintiff. 
38. Dr M Zahir, the learned Senior Advocate in order to substantiate the assertion that the defendants through the owner of the vessel had agreed to settle the cause out of Court, relied upon Exhibit No. 9 which is an alleged agreement executed in between the PW 1, the Managing Director of the plaintiff Company and one Gulilimo Hinojosha Shalgoda witnessed by one Mr Bijoy Chowdhury and Mr Anisuddin Mahmood, and vigorously argued that Exhibit No. 9 clearly revealed that the owner of the ship 'MV Chosun Hope' has settled the claim of the plaintiff, raised in this Admiralty Suit being No 44 of 1997 and if the same cannot recorded as compromise under the provision of Order 23, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 the same ought to treated as an admission of the plaintiff's claim at least upto US$ 40,000. 
39. It appears that Exhibit 9 has not been admitted by the defendants which was drafted on a Bangladesh yellow cartridge paper having embed mark XXIV and nowhere within the four corner of the said agreement it has been mentioned as to the place of its execution which is a vital aspect as to its genuinely as one of the executants is a foreigner. Moreover, none of the attesting witnesses of the said agreement Bijoy Chowdhury or Anisuddin Mahmood have been examined before this Court for the purpose of proving the gentility of execution of Exhibit No. 9. As the defendants categorically denied the execution of this document the onus to prove the same lies on this holder of the plaintiff under the Provision of Section 103 of the Evidence Act, 1872 who did not prove the document while examined as PW 1. Therefore the Exhibit No. 9 is not entitled to be considered by this Court for the purpose of admission by the defendant as to the claim to the plaintiff. Therefore, the argument on this Exhibit No. 9 as advance by the learned Senior Advocate Dr M Zahir falls flat. Accordingly, the issue No. 8 is disposed of in favour of the defendant and against the plaintiff. 
40. In view of the discussion and reasoning as above, this Court finds that the plaintiff succeeds in proving the cause in part for which the plaintiff is entitled to a decree in part in the suit and accordingly this Court hold that the plaintiff is entitled to recover compensation from the defendant No. 1 at an amount of Taka 1,06,250 along with simple interest (at 18% PA form the date of discharge of the cargo upto the actual realization of the decrial dues. 
41. The Court fee paid is sufficient. 
42. Hence, it is ordered. 
That the suit be and hereby decreed in part with cost. The plaintiff is entitled to recover from the defendant No. 1 an amount of Taka 1,06,250 as compensation for short delivery of 8.48 MT of Cargo along with simple interest (a) 18% PA from the date of discharge of the Cargo till actual realization of the decreetal dues along with the cost of this suit and the defendant No. 1 is directed to pay the decreetal amount to the plaintiff or to deposit the same in the Court within 30 days from the date of decree drawn. The office is direct is directed to calculate the interest and the cost and inform the same to the defendant within the date fixed. 
End.

lawyer:
Zainul Abedin with ATM Alamgir with Sadia Arman, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 

Mahbubey Alam with Md Mozammel Hossain with Toufique Anwar Chowdhury, Advocates—For the opposite party Nos.1 and 2.
parties:
Sabera Khatun and others ------ Plaintiff-Petitioners
vs. 
Sena Kalyan  Sangstha and others ------ Defendant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 30-7-2006 (decree signed on 6-8-2006) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 552 of 2002 allowing the appeal and reversing those dated 10-11-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 5 of 2002 decreeing the suit should not be set-aside.

2. The petitioners as plaintiffs brought the aforesaid Other Class Suit No. 68 of 2000 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong impleading the opposite par-ties as defendants for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land and for further declaration that the BS record of right is wrong and that the suit land is not the abandoned property. The suit was subsequently renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 5 of 2002. The case of the plaintiffs in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Fayezulla and others and it was recorded accordingly in their names in RS record of right, who sold the suit land to Yusuf Abdul Karim and handed over possession along with all papers of the suit land to Yusuf Abdul Karim and accordingly the suit land has been recorded in his name being PS Khatian No. 17; that Yusuf Abdul Karim while in possession orally gifted the suit land to his faithful and dutiful personal driver Md Abdur Rahman in 1965, who by spending huge money repaired the building standing on the suit land and extended it by constructing 4 rooms. Later on, Yusuf Abdul Karim by swearing an affidavit on 9-3-1970 confirmed his oral gift to Md Abdur Rahman. The present plaintiff-petitioners are the heirs of Abdur Rahman (now deceased) and they acquired the suit land by inheritance; that Abdur Rahman, the predecessor of the plaintiffs due to his serious illness could not take step for recording the suit land in BS record of right. The plaintiff No. 1 (wife of Abdur Rahman) being a women also could not take any appropriate step for recording the suit land in their name though she learnt from her close relation that the suit land was recorded in the name of Abdur Rahman and so believing it took no other steps but they have been in possession in the suit land for more than 12 years from the time of `their predecessor and the defendants did not put any obstruction so long in the long possession of the suit land by the plaintiffs; that on 2-3-2000 the plaintiff No. 3, Md Fakrul Islam learnt from defendant No.2 that the suit land has been recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 in the BS Khatian and so they would be evicted from the suit land and then the plaintiffs procured a certified copy of the BS Khatian on 3-4-2000 from the local revenue office and came to know about it; that the defendants have got no title, interest and possession in the suit land, who on the basis of wrong record of right are trying to evict the plaintiffs from the suit land and hence, the suit.

3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying most of the allegations of the plaint and contending, inter-alia, that the suit building is a part of Enesel Manson of Chattaswrin Road which is the property of Enesel Textile Mills Limited. According to the memorandum of articles of Nur Sons Ltd. Yusuf Abdul Karim, Rashid, A Karim, Hamid A. Karim and MA Sattar were shareholder directors of it, who left this country during liberation war leaving the suit property as uncared position and thereupon, the Government under the provisions of PO 16 of 1972 declared the suit property as abandoned property; that the Government by a circular on 14-12-1972 handed over the suit property along with other 18 industries to the defendant No. 1, who took possession therein and accordingly BS Khatian in respect of suit property has been recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 correctly and the defendant No. 1 paid rent to the Government up-to 1406 BS; that Abdur Rahman was driver of Nur Sons Ltd. and he used to reside in the suit building and after the death of Abdur Rahman on humanitarian ground the family of Abdur Rahman was permitted to reside therein; that when the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 asked the plaintiffs to vacate the suit land the plaintiffs by creating a false document dated 9-3-1970 instituted the suit falsely and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Assistant Judge on the pleadings of the parties framed the following issues for determination:—

(i) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner?

(ii) Whether the suit is barred by limitation?

(iii) Whether the suit property is Enesel Textile Mills Ltd.?

(iv) Whether the suit property was rightly declared as an abandoned property?

(v) Whether the plaintiff has right, title and possession in the suit land?

(vi) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree?

(vii) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get any other relief?

5. At the trial plaintiff side examined in all 4 witnesses and defendant side examined in all 5 witnesses and both the parties also exhibited some documents to prove their respective cases. The trial Court on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record found the claim of the plaintiffs true and decreed the suit as sought for by judgment and decree dated 10-11-2002.

6. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2, thereupon, preferred Other Class Appeal No. 552 of 2002 before the learned District Judge, Chittagong challenging the legality of the judgment and decree dated 10-11-2002 which was ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong, who was pleased to allow the appeal and set-aside the judgment and decree dated 10-11-2002 by his judgment and decree dated 30-7-2006 on the ground of maintainability of the suit.

7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 30-7-2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 552 of 2002 the present petitioners have come before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

8. Mr Zainul Abedin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in the course of his argument after placing the judgments of two Courts below, deposition of witnesses and other materials on record submits that the learned Judge of the appellate court below misconceived the facts of the case and the judgment of the learned Assistant Judge as well and wrongly set-aside the same. He further submits that the learned Joint District Judge erred in law in reversing the judgment of the Trial Court without properly considering the vital aspect of the case that the suit land as described in the plaint was not enlisted as an abandoned property and the case made out by the plaintiff-petitioners and the same has occasioned failure of justice. Finally, Mr Zainul Abedin with all seriousness criticized the observation of the appellate Court below that the appellate Court below as last court of fact, without adverting the material findings of the trial Court and without properly considering the facts of the case and the case made out by the petitioners had abruptly reversed the findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court on the point of maintainability of the suit in a summary manner and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

9. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that the original owner of the suit property Yusuf Abdul Karim left Bangladesh before liberation leaving the suit property with uncared condition and after liberation the property in question was found abandoned inasmuch as the whereabouts of the owner of the suit property, Yusuf Abdul Karim was not known to the Government and so it was taken over by the Government declaring as an abandoned property and thereafter, the Government transferred the suit property by a registered deed of sale dated 4-10-1980 to Sena Kallyan Sangstha. Mr Mahbubey Alam further submits that it is apparent from the record that the property in question transferred by the Government to Sena Kallyan Sangstha in 1980 and long twenty years after the heirs of Abdur Rahman filed the instant suit claiming the property on the basis of a plea of oral gift without any legal basis whatsoever.

10. Referring to the affidavit dated 9-3-1970 Mr Mahbubey Alam submits that it is the positive case of the plaintiff-petitioners that Yusuf Abdul Karim by swearing an affidavit on 9-3-1970 confirmed his oral gift to Md Abdur Rahman (now deceased), the predecessor of the petitioners which appears to be a forged document inasmuch as the alleged affidavit dated 9-3-1970 clearly shows that stamp purchased in the name of Guru Mia on 20-10-1962 and the same has been done by small letter in a congested manner to complete the document in one page by forging the signature of Yusuf Abdul Karim. He further submits that there is nothing on record to suggest that the so-called oral gift was all acted upon inasmuch as admittedly the plaintiffs or their predecessor, Abdur Rahman neither did pay any rent to the Government nor took any attempt for mutating their name over a period of 30 years and in that view of the matter the learned Additional District Judge was perfectly justified in reversing the judgment and decree of the trail Court on the clear finding that the suit is an abandoned property and as such the suit is not maintainable. Mr Mahbubey Alam further submits that the Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh has transferred Plot Nos. 11, 13 and 17 of Mouza-Joypahar to Sena Kallyan Sangstha on 4-10-1980 by a registered deed treating the same as abandoned property whereas the plaintiffs produced alleged deed of gift claiming the ownership in PS Plot No. 21 without having any valid document whatsoever and the appellate Court below after discussion of evidence on record has rightly come to the conclusion that the trial Court committed wrong in decreeing the suit.

11. Finally, Mr Mahbubey Alam points out that PW-1, Md Fakhrul Islam, son of Abdur Rahman in his cross-examination admitted that PS Plot No. 21 corresponds to BS Plot No. 17 and since Sena Kallyan Sangstha purchased Plot No. 17 in the year 1980 and thus, the claim of the plaintiff-petitioners that holding No.281 does not correspond to the suit land is not at all relevant for deciding the instant suit.

12. Ms Sadia Arman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners to refute the argument of Mr Mahbubey Alam that the appellate court below committed no wrong in holding that the suit is not maintainable upon referring to the order of the trial Court dated 4-6-2002 submits that after filing written statement the defendant-opposite parties filed an application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on 4-6-2002 on the ground that the suit is not maintainable as the suit property is an abandoned property, the trial court below rejected the said application against which the defendants did not prefer any appeal or revision. Ms Sadia Arman, thereafter, upon referring to the schedule of the plaint and gazette notification submits that the land in question mentioned in the gazette notification is not the suit and there is nothing on record to show that the Government formed an opinion as to why the suit land should be declared abandoned property and in that view of the matter the findings of the appellate Court below on the point of maintainability is perverse being contrary to law, evidence and materials on record.

13. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the record including the plaint, the deposition of the witnesses and the impugned judgment as well as judgment of the trial Court. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the learned Advocates for the respective parties it would be convenient for me to decide first of all the maintainability of the suit.

14. On perusal of the record, it appears that the petitioners as plaintiff instituted. Other Class Suit No. 68 of 2000 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land measuring 4 gandas of land along with further declaration that the suit land is not an abandoned property and the BS record of right in respect of the suit land is wrong. It further appears that the defendant-opposite parties after filing written statement filed an application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on 4-6-2002 stating that:

বিবাদী তাহার লিখিত বর্নানায় নালিশী সম্পত্তি পরিত্যক্ত সম্পত্তি হয় ও অত্র মোকদ্দমা পি,ও ১৭/৭২ মতে বারিত বলিয়া আপত্তি উত্থাপন করে।---- এমতাবস্থায় পরিস্থিতিতে অন্যান্য Issue শুনানীর জন্য গৃহীত হওয়ার পূর্বে মোকদ্দমায় রক্ষনীয়তা সম্পর্কে Issue  পূর্বে শুনানীর জন্য গ্রহন করা প্রয়োজন। অন্যথায় বিবাদীর সমূহ ক্ষতি হইবে।

The trial Court below upon hearing the said application by its order No. 51 dated 4-6-2002 rejected the application and admittedly the defendant-opposite   parties did not prefer any appeal or revision against that order dated 4-6-2002.

15. At the trial both the parties led evidence to prove their respective cases. The Trial Court after closing of the evidence and hearing argument of the parties decreed the suit, holding that the plaintiff-petitioners have been able to prove unbroken possession in the suit property for the last 36/37 years and the suit is not barred by any law. In appeal, the learned Joint District Judge, Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-7-2006 set-aside the judgment and decree dated 10-11-2002 mainly on 3(three) counts that : (i) the suit itself is not maintainable as the suit land is an abandoned property (ii) the plaintiffs could not prove their oral gift as well as affidavit with regard to declaration of oral gift and (iii) the plaintiffs did not pay any rent, tax and bill to the Government in respect of the suit land over a period of 32 years i.e. 1970-2002.

16. Now, to justify the finding of the Court of appeal below that the suit itself is not maintainable since the suit property is an abandoned property I feel it necessary to quote hereunder the schedule of the plaint for having a better view of the dispute in question which reads as follows:—

Schedule to the plaint.

জেলা-চট্টগ্রাম, থানা-কোতয়ালী, মৌজা-জয়পাহাড়, আর,এস, খতিয়ান নং-৩২ এর অধীনে আর, এস ১৫ দাগের অন্দর ও তৎসামিলের পি, এস, খতিয়ান নং ৯৭ এর অধীনে পি, এস, ২১ নং দাগের অন্দর তৎসামিলের বি, এস, খতিয়ানের নং-৩৬ এর অধীনে বি, এস, দাগ নং ১ ৭ এর ২০১২ শতক ভূমির অন্দর ৮০০ শতক বা ৪(চার) গন্ডা ভূমি অতিদস্থিত তদন্থিত সেমি পাকা দালানগৃহ খালি জায়গাসহ চিহিৃতমতে দখলীয় বটে।

চক নং-উত্তরে ইউছুপ আব্দুল করিম এর অবশিষ্ট জায়গা, দক্ষিনে-এন, জি, মোবারক ও ডাঃ তৌহিদুল আলম, পূর্বে-সিটি কর্পোরেশনের ড্রেন, পশ্চিমে-জনসাধারনের জন্য সিটি কর্পোরেশনের পথ ।

17. Ms Sadia Arman, the learned Advocate upon referring Ext. 5, tax receipt submits that the suit property as described in the plaint is not an abandoned property inasmuch as the property in question as described in Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986 does not suggest that the suit property is an abandoned property whatsoever. She adds that Ext. 5 tax receipt of City Corporation clearly shows that holding No. 1380/1503 is the suit property belonged to the plaintiff-petitioners.

18. In order to consider whether the suit property as descried in schedule of the plaint let me quote the property in question as described in Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986 which runs as follows:

ক্রমিক নং-৮৬

হোল্ডিং নং

৮৩৫/৯৩৭, বাগমনিরাম (আলফরিদ চেম্বার)

২৮১ চট্রশ্বরী রোড, চট্রগ্রাম।

19. On comparison of the above schedule of the plaint, Exhibit 5, tax receipt of City Corporation and the holding of the property in question as described in Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986 it appears to me that the suit property as described in the plaint and Ext.5 and the property in question as described in the list of the abandoned property of Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986 are not same and similar. Therefore, I find no difficulty whatever in holding that the Court of appeal below was plainly wrong in setting-aside the judgment and decree of the trial court on the ground that the suit was not maintainable since the suit property enlisted as an abandoned property. My view is, therefore, that the finding of the Court of appeal below is a product of non-application of judicial mind and suffers from patent illegality.

20. Having realized the difficulty, Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate at the far end of the hearing upon placing an application under Order XLI, Rule 37 of the Code of Civil Procedure for allowing the opposite parties to adduce additional evidence submits that after commencement of hearing of the instant case Sena Kallyan Sangstha on search found the original copy of the registered sale deed dated 4-10-1980 and the main question now raised before this Court is as to whether the land mentioned in the gazette notification is the suit land or not and for determination of the said issue the sale deed dated 4-10-1980 is required to be admitted as additional evidence.

21. On the contrary, Ms Sadia Arman, the learned Advocate submits that the revisional court may in appropriate cases consider additional evidence, but in the instant case the suit land of the plaintiffs is not abandoned for the allowing reasons:

(a) The plaintiff petitioners are citizens of Bangladesh who came into ownership and possession of the suit land before the PO 16 of 1972 was passed.

(b) The Government formed no opinion as to why the suit land should be declared abandoned.

(c) There is no clear order declaring the suit land as abandoned property. d) There is no demarcation or description of the property that has been declared to be abandoned on any of the documents produced by the defendants.

(e) Although the documents mention Enesel (NSL) Mansion as abandoned, there is no evidence to show that the suit land was ever a part of Enesel Mansion.

f) The plaintiff petitioners received no notification from the Government that the suit land has been declared abandoned and, for these reasons it is needless to admit the sale deed dated 4-10-1980 as additional evidence.

22. Ms Sadia Arman has also emphatically urged another aspect before me that the deed dated 9-3-1970 is more than 30 years old and therefore the Court is entitled to presume that it is a genuine document. More so, under Muslim law, the gift has been made beyond recall, and there was no need to register the gift under the law of those times, when registration was not mandatory as it is today. The learned Advocate also forcefully agitated that even if the said Deed is defective and unregistered, the plaintiffs have been in possession beyond the statutory period of limitation to the complete ouster of the defendants and thus their imperfect title has been perfected by the passage of time.

23. To this, Mr Mahbubey Alam, upon referring a decision reported in 51 DLR (AD) 141 submits that since the document was executed on 4-10-1980 and in the meantime 30(thirty) years time has been passed this Court can admit the same into evidence under Section 90 of the Evidence Act, considering the fact that same was executed on behalf of the president in favour of a statutory organization. He further contends to create an ambiguity regarding identification of the suit land the plaintiffs are now submitting before this Court for the first time that the suit plot has not been made an abundant property though it is apparent from the record that the suit Plot No. 21 was recorded as BS Plot No. 17 which includes land of some other plots showing an area of 2018 acre which has been recorded in the name of Sena Kallyan Sangstha and sale deed dated 4-10-1980 clearly shows the sale of Plot No. 17 along with other plots of Mouza Joypahar and it has been mentioned in the schedule of the plaint BS plot No. 17 with an area of .2012 acre which clearly corresponds to the sale deed dated 4-10-1980 and exhibit Kha BS Khatian of BS plot No. 17 and, as such, to resolve the dispute whether the land mentioned in the gazette notification is the suit land or not and for determination of the said issue the sale deed dated 4-10-1980 is required to be admitted as additional evidence.

24. Finally, Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate submits that the trial Court below decreed the suit on the finding that the enlistment of the suit property in the list of the abandoned property was illegal and defective and the plaintiffs against that finding did not file any revision or appeal before the higher Court and now, it does not lie in the mouth of the plaintiffs that the suit property has been enlisted as an abandoned property.

25. In reply, Ms Sadia Arman submits that in the facts and circumstance of the case the application under Order XLI, Rule 37 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the defendant-opposite parties is plainly misconceived and not tenable in law inasmuch as the defendant-opposite parties had ample opportunity to produce the so-called deed at the trial stage, or even at the appellate stage, and make it an exhibit, but they did not produce any such document and, as such, they cannot be allowed to produce such document before this Revisional Court. She further contends that the defendant-opposite parties did not even produce their deed when the instant Civil revision was filed, six years ago in 2006 and the opposite parties with the sole purpose of delaying the judgment and defeating the ends of justice have produced such document at the judgment stage when all submissions have already been made.

26. It appears that the trail Court after discussion of evidence on record has come to the conclusion that admittedly the plaintiffs as successor of Abdur Rahman are in possession of the suit land over a period of 36/37 years and the suit is not barred by any law and, as such, the plaintiff are entitled to get decree, as prayer for. In coming to this conclusion the trial Court has noticed that the suit property has not been specifically mentioned in exhibit-ka (gazette of the abandoned property).

27. On a query by me Ms Sadia Arman admits that the trial court below committed wrong in observing that the suit property was illegally included in the list of abandoned property. She next submits that from the materials on record it appears that the materials on record justify the judgment and decree of the trial court but the appellate court below without adverting any of the material findings of the trial Court abruptly in a sleep-short manner set-aside judgment of the trial court and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

28. Ms Sadia Arman further submits that the so-called deed of the opposite parties does not show anywhere that any land answering to the description of the suit land was transferred by the Government either with reference to the holding number, or by any other reference and therefore the photocopy of the purported deed is quite redundant to prove any point. The other point agitated by Ms Sadia Arman that there is no reason to send the case back on remand to the lower appellate Court since evidence on all material points are there on record. Ms Sadia Arman to fortify her lengthy argument has relied on the decisions reported in 27 DLR (1975) 170, 40 DLR (AD) 116, 28 DLR (1976) 27, 5 BLC (AD) 76, AIR(33) 1946 Allahabad 389, 8 BLT (AD) 185, 3 BLT 245, PLD 1952 Lahore 545, 10 DLR (WP) 14 = PLD 1957 Lahore 574, AIR 1956 (Andhra) 250, AIR 1957 ( Nagpur )15, 53 DLR (AD) 110, AIR 1991 Supreme Court 2027 (Para 2), AIR 1956 (Andhra) 250, AIR ( 33) 1946 (Allahabad) 389, 7 BLT (1999)195.

29. On a close perusal of the entire evidence and materials on record, it appears that the plaintiff-petitioners for the first time raised before this Court as to whether the land mentioned in the gazette notification is the suit land or not. It further appears that DW1, deposed on behalf of the Sena Kallyan Sangstha who filed a photocopy of the aforesaid deed and stated as follows:

“ বাংলাদেশ সরকার কর্তৃক সেনা কল্যান সংস্থাকে প্রদত্ত নালিশী সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্ত original deed 44 photocopy জমা দিলাম। But the same was not marked as Exhibit. It also appears that defendant, Sena Kallyan Sangstha stated in its written statement that—

“ সরকার ৪-১০-১৯৮০ ও ৩২১৯৮ নং দলিল মূলে এনিসেল ম্যানসেনে তথা মিউনিসিপ্যাল হোল্ডিং নং ৮২১ এবং ১০২৫ আর,এস ১৭/৪৬/১১৯/১২০ খতিয়ানের জমি ও গৃহে সার্ভেন্ট কোয়ার্টার, দারোয়ান কোয়াটার ও ড্রাইভার কোয়ার্টার সহ সেনা কল্যান সংস্থার বরাবরে হস্তান্তর করে।”

30. It is also found that the Government of Bangladesh being defendant No. 3 in the suit did not appear and contest the suit claiming the suit property as abandoned property by producing any paper. Furthermore, the admitted evidence on record both oral and documentary suggests that the suit land has a distinct holding number and there is no demarcation or description of the suit land as described in the plaint has been declared to be an abandoned property

<u>31. On perusal of the judgment of the appellate Court and trial Court below as well it appears that trial Court had considered the material evidence in detail in coming to its finding of title and possession in favour of the plaintiffs, but the appellate Court, without discussing the evidence, had abruptly reversed the findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court on the point of maintainability of the suit. Thus it appears that the impugned judgment of the appellate Court was not a proper judgment of reversal.</u>

32. In view of all the facts noticed above, I am of the view that the case should be decided by taking into consideration the case of the plaintiffs and defendants as well and for the said purpose the defendant, Sena Kallyan Sangstha will be permitted to exhibit registered deed dated 4-10-1980 in accordance with law for determining the real question in controversy. The Court of appeal below shall consider all aspects of the case and decide the appeal afresh. Since the defendant opposite parties are themselves to blame for their predicament but now they are getting a favourable order, they should bear the cost of the plaintiffs in the case.

<u>33. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30-7-2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No.552 of 2002 is set-aside and the case is remanded to the appellate court for deciding the appeal afresh in the light of the observation made above.</u>

34. However, in the facts and circumstance of the case the defendant opposite party No. 1, Sena Kallyan Sangstha is restrained by an order of injunction not to disturb with the peaceful possession of the plaintiff-petitioners in any manner till disposal of the appeal.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:
Ajmalul Hossain QC with Mohammad Saifullah, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 
Md Al-Amin Sarkar, Deputy Attorney-General—For respondent No. 1.
parties:
AKM Enayet Ullah. ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Khurshid Alam Sarkar J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why a direction should not be given for implementation of the government's decision being Memo No. Sol: Misc-15/2008 (Writ)-454 dated 30-4-2009 issued by the Ministry of Law as contained in Annexure-I and the Memo No. Ama/Abi/Probi-7/Bokeya Bhatqa-3/2009(Angsha-2)/146 dated 14-10-2009 issued by the Ministry of Finance as contained in Annexure-K and as to why the inaction of the respondents in respect of keeping the matter pending should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

2. Briefly, facts of the case of the writ petitioner, as stated in the writ petition, are that the petitioner started his carrier as an Assistant Engineer of the East Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation (EPIDC, now known as BIDC) in the year of 1966 and, thereafter, on 30-9-1970 he had the fortune to be in the UK being endowed with a British Government Scholarship for higher studies leading to PhD. It is stated that during liberation war the petitioner was nominated as the President of the Student Action Committee in the UK, which resulted in disruption of his PhD research program and, consequently, was able to complete only MS (Master of Science) in System Control and Management. The petitioner returned to Bangladesh and joined in his service on 5-10-1979 as the Deputy Secretary at the Ministry of Agriculture and Forest with retrospective effect of his appointment in the said post from 16-12-1971.

3. Thereafter, when the respondents without considering the petitioner's case promoted some other officers, who were juniors to the petitioner, to the post of Additional Secretary and subsequently to the post of Secretary on 4-3-1991 and 21-4-1993, respectively, superseding the petitioner, at that point in time, he, in an endeavour to remedy the deprivation and injustice that he had been suffering and thereby for vindication of his lawful rights as to the non-consideration of his case of promotions, postings, financial benefits and other facilities, served a notice demanding justice on 21-7-1993 upon the Ministry of Establishment which triggered a thorough investigation by the National Security Intelligence (NSI) who submitted a comprehensive report to the office of the Hon'ble Prime Minister and the same was forwarded to the office of the Attorney-General who made some recommendations in favour of the petitioner on 23-11-96 in the form of "Case Summary" bearing No. ৬১৩(আই/৯৬-এ,জি (Annexure-A to the writ petition). The learned Attorney-General, then, vide his letter dated 9-12-1997 being ৭৪৫(আই/৯৭ এজি(অং/নং-২) (Annexure-B to the writ petition) provided an update to the learned advocate of the petitioner on the petitioner's case.

4. Thereafter, the petitioner made a number of representations to the respondents but the aforesaid recommendations were not implemented and, eventually, to the petitioner's utter shock, he was sent on retirement on 11-5-2002. Then, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 4124 of 2002 and this Court vide its judgment and order dated 25-6-2003 made the Rule absolute in part by rejecting the petitioner's prayer for interfering with the order of the retirement but directing the respondents to implement the remedial measures as contained in paragraph 8 of the "Case Summary" prepared by the Attorney General and approved by the Hon'ble Prime Minister. (Annexure-A to the instant writ petition). Upon preferring CPLA No. 978 of 2003 the government obtained leave and the Appellate Division vide its judgment and order dated 6-12-2004 in Civil Appeal No. 5 of 2004 set-aside the judgment and order of the High Court Division with the following observation:

"However, from the records and in view of the submissions made by Mr TH Khan, we find that the grievances of the respondent as pointed out by the learned Counsel are no doubt genuine and in our view, this case is a unique one and it is for the Government to consider grievances of the respondent. We also find from the record, that the respondent was a freedom fighter and thoroughly an honest officer but he has been deprived of his legitimate expectation. We, therefore, are of the view that the some in justice has been done to the respondent. We, therefore, like to observe again that the respondent may now approach the Government for consideration of his grievances in the interest of justice and good conscience ".

5. Thereafter, the petitioner filed AT Case No. 163 of 2005 which was dismissed on 16-10-2006 on the ground of maintainability and then he preferred AAT appeal No. 92 of 2007. At the same lime, the petitioner made a written representation on 3-6-2007 to the Hon'ble Chief Advisor praying for implementation of the observation given by the Appellate Division and, on 9-2-2009, another representation was submitted to the Hon'ble Prime Minister who forwarded it to the Ministry of Establishment on 22-3-2009 for taking necessary steps. Then, on 20-4-2009, the said Ministry sought legal opinion on the petitioner's matter from the Ministry of Law and Justice which replied that during pendency of the petitioner's case in the Administrative Tribunal, no opinion could be given and, at this juncture, at the request of the Government, the petitioner withdrew his case and, then, the Law Ministry gave opinion on 30-4-2009 supporting the petitioner's case upon detailing the background of the petitioner's grievance and the remedy available for the petitioner. Thereafter, on 6-9-2009 the Ministry of Establishment vide its Memo No. সূত্রঃ তাহার স্মারক নং-সস(উনি-১)প-/৩২৩-৩৫৪, তাং ২০/৪/০৯ ইং sought opinion from the Ministry of Finance who, in reply, expressed its consent to disburse the required fund in favour of the petitioner vide Memo No. অবি/প্রবি-৭(বকেয়া ভাতা-৩/২০০৯(অংশ)-২/১৪৬ dated 14-10-2009 (Annexure-K to the writ petition) being addressed to the Ministry of Establishment. Thereafter, the petitioner made numerous representations to the respondents for implementation of his entitlements but to no avail. It is stated that there are instances by the present government of granting remedial measures to a number of former Deputy Secretaries, Joint Secretaries and Additional Secretaries who were sent on forced retirement by the previous Government but the petitioner has been denied the same treatment. Hence, this writ petition.

6. Respondent No. 1, Ministry of Public Administration, has entered appearance and contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter-alia, that the erstwhile Ministry of Establishment, which is presently renamed as Ministry of Public Administration, did not refer the matter to the Department of National Security Intelligence (NSI) for carrying out any investigation or did not ask the then learned Attorney-General to provide any opinion on the petitioner's case. The Ministry of Public Administration is not aware of the said correspondence at all and, more importantly, any report of NSI and comments of the then learned Attorney-General have nothing to do with the matter. However, after the present government assumed power the matter of the petitioner was referred to the Ministry of Finance for their opinion and it did not provide any specific recommendation, rather opined that the issue could not be considered with the reference to the case of other persons. Furthermore, the Ministry of Public Administration cannot consider the issue of the petitioner as per the opinion of the Ministry of Finance because the context of the petitioner is quite different from the issue referred to by the Ministry of Finance and, therefore, the claim of the petitioner that Ministry of Finance recommended in his favour is not true.

7. It is stated that the petitioner's case for promotion as a Secretary was placed to the Superior Selection Board (SSB) at different times with facts and records. In the meetings of SSB held on different dates, he was not found fit for promotion. The cases of the other officers, who were referred to as the instances in his writ petition, were quite different from the petitioner's case. It is also stated that the petitioner joined in the Government service as ex-cadre on 5-10-1979 and, thereafter, he was promoted to the posts of Joint Secretary and Additional Secretary. He went to retirement on 9-1-2002 and now he is no more in the Government service. The petitioner previously filed Writ Petition No. 4124 of 2002 challenging his retirement order and seeking direction for the implementation of the remedial measures recommended by the then Attorney-General and the High Court Division vide its judgment and order dated 25-6-03 declined to interfere with the order of retirement but directed the government to implement the remedial measures recommended by the then Attorney-General. However, when the government preferred Civil Appeal No. 5 of 2004, the Appellate Division set-aside the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division on the ground that the petitioner's issues do not fit in the writ jurisdiction. Thereafter, the petitioner filed AT Case No. 163 of 2005 before the Administrative Tribunal which was rejected on 1-10-2006 when the petitioner preferred AAT No. 92 of 2007 before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal but the said appeal was withdrawn on 2-6-2009 by the petitioner himself. It is stated that the present writ petition involves the same issues of the previous Writ Petition No. 4124 of 2012 and the AT Case No. 163 of 2005 in which the petitioner was unsuccessful.

8. Mr Ajmalul Hossain QC, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, places Article 117 of the Constitution before us and submits that this writ is fully maintainable and the Constitution does not create a bar to this writ petition inasmuch as the petitioner has been in the service of the Republic historically and, at present, he is no longer in the service of the Republic and, as such, his grievances do not relate to the terms and condition of his service, rather he is seeking justice for the injustices he suffered while serving the Republic. In a bid to substantiate his above contention, he placed the chronology of events of the petitioner's case in the manner as stated hereinbefore and upon dealing with each of the phases of the petitioner's service life and the events took place after sending him on retirement, Mr Hossain submits that the focus of his case is no longer on grievances during his service years, rather, the focus is now on the government's acknowledgement that injustices were done to him and he should have redress thereto. He submits that in view of the fact that no redress has been given by the government the petitioner, having exhausted all avenues and there being no place he can turn to, has rightly approached this Court.

9. He went on to interpret Article 117 (1) of the Constitution and submits that it specifically deals with the setting up of tribunals with jurisdiction relating to terms and conditions of service of persons in the service of the Republic, including matters in Part IX and awards of penalties and punishments. Part IX deals with the appointments and conditions of service, tenure of office, dismissal, removal, reduction in rank, and recognisation of service and submits that there is nothing in Article 117(1) that applies to this case.

10. He submits that Article 117(2) also does not apply to the petitioner's case inasmuch as it imposes the legal bar in respect of any matter within the jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal and upon placing section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 before us, he submits that jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal is given in respect of (a) person in the service of the Republic including someone who is dismissed or retired, (b) in respect of terms and conditions of his service including pension rights or in respect of any order made or decision or action taken, which are, apparently, all about orders, decisions, actions but not about inaction, failure to act or omissions. The petitioner in this writ petition is challenging the inaction or failure to act on the part of the government on its decision and seeks for an order of mandamus. In a bid to substantiate his above submission as to meaning of action, he refers to the case of Abdul Mannan Talukder vs Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation reported in 42 DLR (AD) 104 and submits that since there is no order, decision or action against the petitioner, he cannot go to the Administrative Tribunal as it will have no jurisdiction. He further submits the cause of action arose long after his service ended and has no relation to it and facts do not relate to any action.

11. He also submits that the Appellate Division conceded to the fact of doing grave injustice to the petitioner by the respondents but observed that it should be remedied by the government and, accordingly, when he approached the government, it agreed to rectify their deeds but did nothing till date. He quotes the maxim "Ibi jus ubiremedium" and submits that if there is a right, there must be a remedy and, as such, the petitioner is entitled to remedial action, which is necessary to complete the process and remove the injustice.

12. He submits that Prime Minister is the Chief Executive of all the ministry and the head of the government and since the two Ministries of the government i.e. Ministry of Law and Justice and Ministry of Finance have taken steps in pursuant to the order of the Hon'ble Prime Minister to cure the injury done to the petitioner, the Ministry of Public Administration has no option but to implement it as the government is estopped by the doctrine of estoppel to change its position.

13. He refers to Annexure-I series to the writ petition and submits that a number of freedom fighter civil servants, who were sent on forced retirement by the previous government being deprived of their deserving promotions, were compensated by the present government in the form of retrospective seniority and other financial entitlements but the petitioner has not been treated in the same manner, which is a clear violation of Articles 27 and 29 of the Constitution. By referring to the case of Mazibur Rahman vs the Bangladesh 44 DLR (AD) 111 and the case of Abdul Awal Munshi (Md) vs Bangladesh Water Development Board, 6 BLC 463, he submits that if, allegation of fundamental right is brought by any citizen, then writ jurisdiction is the only appropriate forum and in view of the fact that the petitioner has been subjected to the sheer discrimination being not treated equally with others, his present petition is maintainable. Finally, he refers to the case of government of Bangladesh vs Jahangir Alam reported in 17 BLC (AD) 115 and submits that it has been the legitimate expectation of the petitioner that the government will act in accordance with its promise made to the petitioner from time to time.

14. Mr Md Al-Amin Sarkar, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the report submitted by the NSI and the "Case Summary" with the recommendation for remedial measures prepared by the then learned Attorney-General are uncalled for as the matter is purely administrative matters which falls within the purview and jurisdiction of the Ministry of Public Administration and the same is not binding upon the respondents.

15.
